title: Academy of Eternal Destiny
tagline: Two towers. One storybook. One sunset.

ui.noItems: Nothing yet. Look around the room.
ui.noTruths: No truths yet. Finish a room to learn one.
ui.holdHelp: Now tap the right spot in the room.
ui.needItem: You need something for this. Open the notebook and hold an item.

mission.kicker: Lumen Spire and Umbral Spire, sunset
mission.heading: The Eternal Storybook Chose
paras: You are Wren of Lumen Spire and Dax of Umbral Spire. One academy, two towers, and at sunset the Eternal Storybook rewrites two students' fates.
It picked you: best friends, one hero and one villain-in-training. The Storybook means to write you apart.
Collect the Quill's three Story Sigils and reach Destiny Tower within five minutes to write your own ending.

tutorial.text: Drag to look around the room. Tap anything that looks like it belongs to the story.
Items and clues you find go into your notes. Open them any time to read them or hold an item.
Finds and solved puzzles earn Story Points. A wrong answer costs 10 and locks the panel for 3 seconds. Close any puzzle with the X.
You have 3 hints for the whole game, 25 Story Points each. The 5:00 clock runs while you puzzle; it only pauses when Wren and Dax talk alone.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Dax... did the Storybook just say our names?

dialogue.speaker: dax
dialogue.text: Both of them. Hero and villain, best friends, and it wants to split us up. Hard pass.

dialogue.speaker: orrin
dialogue.text: Five minutes, little fates. Then the Storybook inks you apart. I will be listening through the speaking-stone.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Then we collect the Quill's three Sigils and write our own ending. Let's move.

dialogue.speaker: orrin
dialogue.text: Tick, tock, little fates. Even the speaking-stone is yawning.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: The Hall of Two Gates. Lumen on the left, Umbral on the right, and the first Sigil hidden somewhere between.

dialogue.speaker: dax
dialogue.text: The floor is split in two halves. I bet it wants us to sort something. Read every plaque first.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: A Lumen pin. Its little star is cold, like it needs a flame.

dialogue.speaker: dax
dialogue.text: An Umbral pin. It hums like a bad idea. I like it already.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: The sconce flares pearl-white, and a plaque shines out of the wall.

dialogue.speaker: dax
dialogue.text: Green fire! And another plaque comes out of the dark.

dialogue.speaker: dax
dialogue.text: The floor split open and the first Sigil rose from the seam. One down, two to go.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: The plaques said both towers prize courage and loyalty. We were never that different, Dax.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Light the Lumen sconce with the Lumen pin, and the Umbral brazier with the Umbral pin. Then read every plaque: only heroes, only villains, and both.

dialogue.speaker: dax
dialogue.text: Not quite. Check the plaques again. What do both towers share?

dialogue.speaker: orrin
dialogue.text: Oh dear. Sorted wrong, and in front of the whole hall.

dialogue.speaker: dax
dialogue.text: The Storybook Library. Every book in here has an opinion about us.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: A wall spell, torn story cards and a huge mirror. Something here only reads true in the glass.

dialogue.speaker: dax
dialogue.text: Reading spectacles. Dust is this library's real guardian.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: A jar of glowmoths. They will light any dark corner.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: The dust is gone. The spell is written backwards. Mirror writing!

dialogue.speaker: dax
dialogue.text: The alcove lit up and the torn story pages came fluttering down.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: The code clicked, the cards flew into order, and Sigil two slid out of the shelf.

dialogue.speaker: dax
dialogue.text: The spell only made sense once we read it the other way round. Maybe endings can be turned round too.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Clean the tapestry with the spectacles. Its spell reads true only in the big mirror, so flip every line. For the cards: the key comes first, the happy ending last.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: That is not it. Read the spell the way the mirror would show it.

dialogue.speaker: orrin
dialogue.text: Mirrors never lie, little hero. Only you do.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: The Potion and Beast Workshop. And that glow-wisp in the cage is crying.

dialogue.speaker: dax
dialogue.text: Cauldrons, cages and tangled rope. Honestly my favourite room. But we free the wisp first.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Fang-proof gloves. Handy around thorns.

dialogue.speaker: dax
dialogue.text: Silver shears. For things that bite, or sparkle.

dialogue.speaker: dax
dialogue.text: The thorns parted and a warden's note fell out.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: The cupboard clicked open. The vials are labelled!

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: The ropes fell loose and the wisp swirled free. It left the third Sigil in my hands.

dialogue.speaker: dax
dialogue.text: It was never trapped, only tangled. We kept pulling when we should have looked.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: You need exactly four measures with the three and five vials: fill the big one, pour it into the small one. Then drag the cage pegs until no rope crosses.

dialogue.speaker: dax
dialogue.text: Wrong measure. Count what stays behind in the big vial.

dialogue.speaker: orrin
dialogue.text: Splash. That is the sound of a failing apprentice.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Destiny Tower. The Storybook is right there, and it is listening.

dialogue.speaker: dax
dialogue.text: Three sockets for three Sigils. Then we open the book and draw our sign in the stars.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: The Sigil sinks in with a soft chime.

dialogue.speaker: dax
dialogue.text: The page is ours. Whatever we write, we write it together.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: The Storybook never wanted to split us. It just never learned that friends can choose.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: Put each Sigil in its socket. The margin note says which true letter sits under L. Then draw the sign from the moon banner: two peaks joined by a bridge, with one star below.

dialogue.speaker: dax
dialogue.text: Check the margin note. The wheel has to turn exactly right.

dialogue.speaker: orrin
dialogue.text: Tut tut. The Storybook is losing patience, and so am I.

dialogue.speaker: wren
dialogue.text: We did it, Dax. Our ending.

dialogue.speaker: dax
dialogue.text: Our ending. Together.

dialogue.speaker: orrin
dialogue.text: The speaking-stone goes quiet. For the first time, so do I.

lumenpin.name: Lumen Pin
lumenpin.text: A pin from the Lumen tower. Its tiny star is cold and wants a flame.

umbralpin.name: Umbral Pin
umbralpin.text: A pin from the Umbral tower. It hums softly and smells of green smoke.

feather.name: Swan Feather
feather.text: Fell from the carved swans over the Lumen Gate. Heroes sign their oaths with feathers like this.

ticket.name: Sealed Letter
ticket.text: A letter sealed with the crests of both towers. It was meant for two friends who never opened it.

spectacles.name: Reading Spectacles
spectacles.text: Wiped clean, they see through the dust of old tapestries.

foxkey.name: Silver Fox Key
foxkey.text: A key shaped like a fox cub. The very first page of a story has one just like it.

ribbon.name: Bookmark Ribbon
ribbon.text: A violet ribbon, marked at the page where two friends meet in a garden.

glowjar.name: Glowmoth Jar
glowjar.text: Tiny moths that glow wherever the dark is thickest.

ladle.name: Copper Ladle
ladle.text: Dented from stirring too many cauldrons. It is not for biting dragons.

phial.name: Moonwater Phial
phial.text: Water caught under last night's full moon. The wisp loves its taste.

gloves.name: Fang-proof Gloves
gloves.text: Stitched thick enough to handle thorn-vines and cranky hatchlings.

tongs.name: Silver Shears
tongs.text: For snipping things that sparkle, sting or bite. They also pick odd cupboard locks.

locket.name: Friendship Locket
locket.text: Inside are two tiny sketches: a hero with a lantern, a villain with a raven.

compass.name: Fate Compass
compass.text: The needle ignores north. It points at whoever matters most to you.

hourglass.name: Sunset Hourglass
hourglass.text: The sand inside never runs out, but it always runs slowly toward sunset.

starchart.name: Star Chart
starchart.text: A chart of the Destiny Tower's ceiling. Someone has circled two peaks and a bridge.

sigil1.name: Sigil of Light
sigil1.text: The first of the Quill's three Story Sigils. It glows warm, like a lantern in a window.

sigil2.name: Sigil of Shadow
sigil2.text: The second Sigil. It sparkles acid-green when nobody is looking.

sigil3.name: Sigil of Ink
sigil3.text: The third Sigil. It belongs to neither tower and both.

truths: Heroes and villains share more than the towers admit: courage and loyalty belong to both.
A story can be read backwards, and its ending can still be turned round.
What looks trapped is often only tangled. Patience frees what force cannot.
Friends write the best endings, because they write them together.

r1venn.help: Tap a trait, then tap Hero, Both or Villain. Tap a placed trait to pick it up again.
r1venn.wrongText: Some trait sits in the wrong circle. Reread the plaques.

r2code.help: Tap a wheel to turn it. The wall spell gives the code in order, top to bottom.

r2order.help: Tap the torn story cards in the order the story happens.

items.label: The fox cub finds a silver key
The key opens a hidden garden

r2order.wrongText: The cards fly apart. Think about what must happen first.

r3pour.help: Measure exactly 4 measures of moonwater. Fill, empty or pour between the two vials.

r3untangle.help: Drag the pegs. Free the wisp by making sure no rope crosses another.

r4cipher.help: Turn the inner ring with the arrows until the runes match the margin note, then confirm.
r4cipher.wrongText: The runes do not line up yet.

r4stars.help: Tap two stars to draw a line between them. Tap them again to erase it. Draw the friends' sign.
r4stars.wrongText: The stars flicker out. That is not their sign.

r4story.help: The Storybook is open at its last page. How does your story end?

options.label: Good
options.text: A bright ending for both towers.
options.closing: Wren wrote the Light ending: the two Spires opened their gates to each other, and Dax, grumbling, carried the first lantern across.

options.label: Evil
options.text: A dark ending, full of cunning.
options.closing: Dax wrote the Shadow ending: the Umbral Spire rose as the grandest tower of all, and Wren, its only hero, still outwitted everyone in it.

options.label: Write Your Own
options.closing: Together they wrote a brand new first line: "Two friends, one academy, and no fate but their own." The Storybook closed softly, and for the first time, it smiled.

rooms.name: Hall of Two Gates
rooms.objective: Find the first Sigil. Read the plaques and sort the traits.
rooms.objectiveReady: Sort the traits on the floor.

reward.toast: The first Sigil rises from the floor.

hotspots.label: Lumen plaque
hotspots.title: Lumen Plaque
hotspots.text: Lumen heroes keep their word, heal the wounded and fight fair.

hotspots.label: Umbral plaque
hotspots.title: Umbral Plaque
hotspots.text: Umbral villains are cunning, ambitious and happy to bend the rules.

hotspots.label: Plaque between the gates
hotspots.title: Plaque Between the Gates
hotspots.text: Hero or villain, every student in this hall is brave and loyal to a friend.

hotspots.label: Headmistress's note
hotspots.title: Headmistress's Note
hotspots.text: Do not sort students by tower colour. Sort by trait: what only heroes are, what only villains are, and what both are.

hotspots.label: Sorceress of Umbral
hotspots.title: Sorceress of Umbral
views: A stone sorceress, her staff tipped with acid-green flame. She smiles like she knows your secrets.
At her feet someone scratched: "Even villains need a friend."
hotspots.secret: Every villain began as someone who just wanted to be chosen.

rooms.name: Storybook Library
rooms.objective: Find the second Sigil. Crack the mirror spell and put the story in order.
rooms.objectiveReady: Use the spell and the pages.

reward.toast: The second Sigil slides out of the shelf.

hotspots.label: Mirror frame
hotspots.title: Frame Inscription
hotspots.text: The looking-glass tells what the wall cannot. Read every line of the wall spell the way it would look in this mirror.

hotspots.label: Wall spell
hotspots.title: Wall Spell
hotspots.text:
The Raven counted its treasures and wrote them on the wall, line by line, top to bottom:
SEVEN CROWS

TWO KEYS

NINE ROSES

ONE MOON

hotspots.label: Floating book
hotspots.title: Torn Page: Beginning
hotspots.text: The silver key comes first of all. Every story starts with a key.

hotspots.label: Floating page
hotspots.title: Torn Page: Middle
hotspots.text: The garden must be unlocked before the rose can sing, and the rose sings its warning before the dragon is tamed.

hotspots.label: Floating book
hotspots.title: Torn Page: End
hotspots.text: The very last page: the garden blooms for everyone.

hotspots.label: Gilt looking-glass
hotspots.title: The Looking-Glass
views: A tall gilt mirror. The library inside it is the same, but every book is turned the other way.
In the glass, Wren stands on Dax's side, and Dax on Wren's. From here, you cannot tell hero from villain.
hotspots.secret: In a mirror, left becomes right, and every story can be read the other way.

rooms.name: Potion and Beast Workshop
rooms.objective: Find the third Sigil. Calm the wisp and free it.
rooms.objectiveReady: Measure the moonwater and free the wisp.

reward.toast: The wisp leaves the third Sigil behind.

hotspots.label: Open recipe book
hotspots.title: Wisp Calming Draught
hotspots.text: Exactly 4 measures of moonwater, no more and no less. Too much drowns the glow; too little leaves it sad.

hotspots.label: Vial labels
hotspots.title: Measuring Vials
hotspots.text: The small vial holds 3 measures and the large vial holds 5. The cauldron can refill either one.

hotspots.label: Feeding chart
hotspots.title: Beast Feeding Chart
hotspots.text: Wisps feed on moonlight, dragons on embers, and every tangle on patience.

hotspots.label: Warden's note
hotspots.title: Cage Warden's Note
hotspots.text: The cage ropes are not knotted, only tangled. Move the pegs until no rope crosses another.

hotspots.label: Dragon cage
hotspots.title: The Hatchling Cage
views: Two sleepy hatchlings, one ember-red and one slate-grey, share a cage and a blanket.
Their cage is tied with the same rope pattern as the wisp's.
hotspots.secret: Their names are scratched on the bars: "Wren" and "Dax".

rooms.name: Destiny Tower
rooms.objective: Set the three Sigils, open the Storybook and write your ending.
rooms.objectiveReady: Open the Storybook and write your ending.

hotspots.label: Sun banner
hotspots.title: Quill's Margin Note
hotspots.text: In the Storybook's margin the Quill scribbled: "Under the rune L, the true letter I waits." Turn the wheel until they line up.

hotspots.label: Moon banner
hotspots.title: The Friends' Sign
hotspots.text: Wren and Dax scratched it on every desk: two peaks joined by a bridge, with one star below.<svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="150" height="150" style="display:block;margin:8px auto;background:rgba(0,0,30,.4);border-radius:12px;border:1.5px solid var(--edge2)"><g stroke="#fbe3dc" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-linecap="round" fill="none"><path d="M15 78L30 28L50 52L70 28L85 78M50 52L50 86"/></g><g fill="#e9a897"><circle cx="15" cy="78" r="3.5"/><circle cx="30" cy="28" r="3.5"/><circle cx="50" cy="52" r="3.5"/><circle cx="70" cy="28" r="3.5"/><circle cx="85" cy="78" r="3.5"/><circle cx="50" cy="86" r="3.5"/></g></svg>

hotspots.label: Lumen tower
hotspots.title: Warden Orrin's Slip
hotspots.text: "The Storybook may only be rewritten by two who agree to write it together."

hotspots.label: White throne
hotspots.title: Throne of Light
views: A pearl-white throne with a golden sun on its back.
Under the cushion someone left a small drawing of a raven.
hotspots.secret: The raven has a little lantern tied to its leg.

cinematic: The three Sigils blaze. The Eternal Storybook turns to its last blank page.

cinematic.fallback: Together they wrote a brand new first line, and the Storybook closed softly.

cinematic: Sunset fades. In the Academy of Eternal Destiny both towers are quiet, and two friends walk down the stairs together.

win.title: Fate Rewritten
win.text: Wren and Dax closed the Eternal Storybook on their own terms.

timeup.title: The Storybook Closed
timeup.text: Sunset ended before the ending was written. The Storybook will try again. So can you.
